title: Two Faces, One Flag
endLine: A lipid's charge and its side of the membrane set its job.

scenes.tts: Straight and kinked tails set how stiff a membrane is, and cholesterol buffers it. Now watch a macrophage glide over a row of cells. It passes healthy cells by, then swallows a dying one before it bursts. What is it reading?
scenes.narration: Straight and kinked tails set how stiff a membrane is, and cholesterol buffers it. Now watch a macrophage glide over a row of cells. It passes healthy cells by, then swallows a dying one before it bursts. What is it reading?
scenes.caption: Straight and kinked tails set how stiff a membrane is, and cholesterol buffers it. Now watch a macrophage glide over a row of cells. It passes healthy cells by, then swallows a dying one before it bursts. What is it reading?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's colour map: BLUE = straight saturated tails, YELLOW = kinked cis tails, GREEN = cholesterol, GREY = glycerol backbones only. New in this film, one colour per concept: phosphatidylcholine (PC) heads WHITE circles (neutral, no sign); phosphatidylserine (PS) heads MAGENTA circles each with a small white minus sign; flippase pumps ORANGE doors spanning the bilayer; scramblases PURPLE doors with a two-way arrow; positively charged cytoplasmic proteins CYAN rounded blobs with a plus sign; the macrophage a large pale PINK cell outline with a soft wobbling edge; phosphatidylinositol (PI) heads TEAL circles; glycolipid sugars short LIME bead chains standing up from the outer face (beads only, never ring structures). THE WORLD, kept all film: a wide horizontal bilayer band crosses the frame and fills about 60% of its height. Top edge = outer leaflet heads, bottom edge = inner leaflet heads, tails pointing into the core, BLUE and YELLOW tails mixed as in the first film, a few GREEN cholesterol pegs in the core. Above the band a dark region labelled 'outside'; below it a slightly tinted region labelled 'cytoplasm'. Slow ambient motion all film: tails flex gently (fluid membrane), heads jiggle sideways, faint particles drift outside. On the first sentence only, tails visibly flex and one GREEN cholesterol peg pulses (recap). In this opening shot every head is a plain GREY circle, as in the first film; the band is drawn as one segment of a longer membrane, with a vertical faint seam marking three neighbouring cells along it. On 'glide', the PINK macrophage enters from the left above the band and slides right along the outer surface. It drifts past the first two cell segments without stopping. Over the third segment it pauses, a dashed outline labelled 'dying cell' appears on that segment, and the macrophage's edge wraps toward it (do not finish the engulfing). On the question, white text across the top: 'What is it reading?' The macrophage rewinds back to the left edge and waits there.

Title 'Two Faces, One Flag' fades in above the band for 2 s while the question text fades out. Tails keep flexing; the PINK macrophage idles at the left edge; the 'dying cell' outline fades away (all three segments look healthy again).

scenes.tts: The answer is not in the tails. It is in the heads. A head group sets a lipid's charge. Phosphatidylcholine carries no net charge, and it is enriched in the outer leaflet. Phosphatidylserine, or P S, is negative. It is held on the inner leaflet.
scenes.narration: The answer is not in the tails. It is in the heads. A head group sets a lipid's charge. Phosphatidylcholine carries no net charge, and it is enriched in the outer leaflet. Phosphatidylserine, or PS, is negative. It is held on the inner leaflet.
scenes.caption: The answer is not in the tails. It is in the heads. A head group sets a lipid's charge. Phosphatidylcholine carries no net charge, and it is enriched in the outer leaflet. Phosphatidylserine, or PS, is negative. It is held on the inner leaflet.
scenes.visual: Camera eases in so one cell's stretch of membrane fills the frame (band still about 60% of frame height). On 'not in the tails', the tails dim slightly; on 'in the heads', both head rows brighten. On 'Phosphatidylcholine', most GREY heads in the TOP row turn WHITE, label 'PC: no net charge' above them. On 'Phosphatidylserine', a scattering of GREY heads in the BOTTOM row turn MAGENTA with minus signs, label 'PS: negative' below them. The other bottom-row heads stay GREY. No MAGENTA heads in the top row. Labels at size 28 or larger. The macrophage is out of frame from here until s08.

scenes.tts: Held is the right word, because pumps keep it there. Flippases spend A T P to move particular lipids to the inner leaflet. Floppases also use A T P, and move lipids outward. Scramblases, when switched on, let lipids cross both ways. In this healthy cell, they stay off.
scenes.narration: Held is the right word, because pumps keep it there. Flippases spend ATP to move particular lipids to the inner leaflet. Floppases also use ATP, and move lipids outward. Scramblases, when switched on, let lipids cross both ways. In this healthy cell, they stay off.
scenes.caption: Held is the right word, because pumps keep it there. Flippases spend ATP to move particular lipids to the inner leaflet. Floppases also use ATP, and move lipids outward. Scramblases, when switched on, let lipids cross both ways. In this healthy cell, they stay off.
scenes.visual: Two ORANGE flippase doors stand in the band, spanning both leaflets. On 'Flippases spend', a small ORANGE token labelled 'ATP' enters a door from the cytoplasm side and pops; one MAGENTA head that had drifted into the top row is carried through the door down into the bottom row. This repeats once more during the scene. On 'Floppases', a third, smaller ORANGE door labelled 'floppase' carries one WHITE head from the bottom row up to the top row, with its own 'ATP' token. On 'Scramblases', a PURPLE door with a two-way arrow appears, labelled 'scramblase: off', drawn dim and closed; it stays dim and closed until s08.

scenes.tts: So the inner face carries negative P S, and positively charged proteins in the cytoplasm meet it there. Phosphatidylinositol sits inside too. Phospholipase C cuts its phosphorylated form, P I P two, into two messengers.
scenes.narration: So the inner face carries negative PS, and positively charged proteins in the cytoplasm meet it there. Phosphatidylinositol sits inside too. Phospholipase C cuts its phosphorylated form, PIP2, into two messengers.
scenes.caption: So the inner face carries negative PS, and positively charged proteins in the cytoplasm meet it there. Phosphatidylinositol sits inside too. Phospholipase C cuts its phosphorylated form, PIP2, into two messengers.
scenes.visual: Camera tilts down toward the inner face. Two CYAN blobs with plus signs drift up from the cytoplasm and settle against the MAGENTA heads, label 'positive proteins'. On 'Phosphatidylinositol', two GREY heads in the bottom row turn TEAL, label 'PI'. On 'P I P two', one of them gains two small dots, label 'PIP2'; a small scissors icon labelled 'phospholipase C' snips it: one small token labelled 'IP3' drifts into the cytoplasm, while the lipid part left in the inner leaflet is labelled 'DAG'. Then the scissors, tokens and PI labels fade; the PI heads stay TEAL.

scenes.tts: The outer face, the one the macrophage meets, looks different. It is rich in P C and in sphingomyelin. Glycolipids sit here too, and their sugars face outward only. Those sugars are the cell's name tag.
scenes.narration: The outer face, the one the macrophage meets, looks different. It is rich in PC and in sphingomyelin. Glycolipids sit here too, and their sugars face outward only. Those sugars are the cell's name tag.
scenes.caption: The outer face, the one the macrophage meets, looks different. It is rich in PC and in sphingomyelin. Glycolipids sit here too, and their sugars face outward only. Those sugars are the cell's name tag.
scenes.visual: Camera tilts up to the outer face. The WHITE PC heads fill the top row. On 'sphingomyelin', a few top-row heads become WHITE squares (same white, square shape), label 'sphingomyelin'. On 'glycolipids', a few top-row heads sprout short LIME bead chains pointing up into the outside region (plain beads, no ring structures), label 'sugars: outward only'. On 'name tag', the LIME chains pulse once. No MAGENTA anywhere on the top row. Camera eases back so both faces are in view; the CYAN proteins still sit under the inner face.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. A head group sets a lipid's charge. Pumps, spending A T P, set which face it sits on. Charge and location together set what the lipid does.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. A head group sets a lipid's charge. Pumps, spending ATP, set which face it sits on. Charge and location together set what the lipid does.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. A head group sets a lipid's charge. Pumps, spending ATP, set which face it sits on. Charge and location together set what the lipid does.
scenes.visual: Hold the whole band, both faces visible. On 'sets a lipid's charge', the WHITE and MAGENTA heads glow in turn; on 'Pumps set which face', the ORANGE flippase doors glow and one more MAGENTA head is carried down; on 'Charge and location together', the MAGENTA heads and the CYAN proteins meeting them glow together, and the LIME sugars glow on the top face. Label centred under the band, size 34: 'charge + side = job'.

scenes.tts: Now this cell begins to die by apoptosis. Its flippases shut off, so P S is no longer pumped back inside. Scramblases switch on, and lipids start crossing both ways, erasing the difference between the faces.
scenes.narration: Now this cell begins to die by apoptosis. Its flippases shut off, so PS is no longer pumped back inside. Scramblases switch on, and lipids start crossing both ways, erasing the difference between the faces.
scenes.caption: Now this cell begins to die by apoptosis. Its flippases shut off, so PS is no longer pumped back inside. Scramblases switch on, and lipids start crossing both ways, erasing the difference between the faces.
scenes.visual: The 'charge + side = job' label fades. Tag at top left: 'apoptosis'. On 'flippases shut off', the ORANGE doors dim to outlines and a small cross appears on each; 'ATP' tokens stop arriving. On 'Scramblases switch on', the PURPLE door brightens and opens, its label changes to 'scramblase: on'. Heads of both colours begin to drift through it in both directions; several MAGENTA heads arrive in the TOP row and stay there. The tails keep flexing.

scenes.tts: The macrophage glides back along the surface, past the healthy cells. What will it now find on the dying cell's outer face?
scenes.narration: The macrophage glides back along the surface, past the healthy cells. What will it now find on the dying cell's outer face?
scenes.caption: The macrophage glides back along the surface, past the healthy cells. What will it now find on the dying cell's outer face?
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the opening view: three cell segments along the band, the dying one in the middle of the frame. The PINK macrophage enters from the left above the band and slides toward it. The new MAGENTA heads in the dying cell's top row are kept small and partly hidden behind a soft haze over the top row (the answer is not yet shown). Question card at top in white: 'What does it find?'

Predict pause. The question card stays. The macrophage hovers just above the dying cell's outer face, edge wobbling slowly. The PURPLE scramblase stays open, heads drifting through it slowly. No other change.

scenes.tts: Phosphatidylserine, now on the outside. The macrophage reads outer P S as an eat me signal. It engulfs the dying cell early, before the cell bursts and inflames the tissue. Its healthy neighbours keep their P S inside.
scenes.narration: Phosphatidylserine, now on the outside. The macrophage reads outer PS as an eat me signal. It engulfs the dying cell early, before the cell bursts and inflames the tissue. Its healthy neighbours keep their PS inside.
scenes.caption: Phosphatidylserine, now on the outside. The macrophage reads outer PS as an eat me signal. It engulfs the dying cell early, before the cell bursts and inflames the tissue. Its healthy neighbours keep their PS inside.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves and the haze lifts: the MAGENTA heads on the dying cell's outer face light up, label 'PS outside'. On 'eat me signal', a label 'eat me' appears beside them. The macrophage's edge touches the MAGENTA heads, then flows around the dying cell's segment and closes over it. On 'healthy neighbours', the two neighbouring segments glow briefly: WHITE heads on top, MAGENTA heads only on the bottom row, ORANGE flippases still working; the macrophage leaves them untouched.

scenes.tts: So the flag was there all along, on the inner face. Pumps spending A T P kept it there. A dying cell writes no new message. It simply moves an old one to the other face.
scenes.narration: So the flag was there all along, on the inner face. Pumps spending ATP kept it there. A dying cell writes no new message. It simply moves an old one to the other face.
scenes.caption: So the flag was there all along, on the inner face. Pumps spending ATP kept it there. A dying cell writes no new message. It simply moves an old one to the other face.
scenes.visual: Return to one healthy cell segment, both faces in view. A MAGENTA head on the inner face glows, label 'the flag, kept inside'; an ORANGE flippase door glows with an 'ATP' token entering it. On 'moves an old one to the other face', a ghost copy of that MAGENTA head slides up through the faded PURPLE door to the outer face, glows, and fades out again; the real head stays inside.

End card over the dimmed but still moving membrane world (tails flexing, WHITE heads on top, MAGENTA heads below, an ORANGE flippase pulsing slowly). Large centred white text: 'A lipid's charge and its side of the membrane set its job.'
